claims.evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental calcium imaging data.

claims.claim: The proportion of warm-sensitive cells was similar in both mouse and squirrel POA.
claims.source: The difference was specific to cold-sensing neurons because the proportion of warm-sensitive cells was similar in both mouse and squirrel POA (mice: 15.2 ± 3.7%, squirrels: 15.1 ± 3.1%, p>0.05, Mann-Whitney test, Figure 1D and E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental calcium imaging data presented in Figure 1.

claims.claim: The difference in cold-sensitive neurons between mice and squirrels is specific to cold-sensing neurons.
claims.source: The difference was specific to cold-sensing neurons because the proportion of warm-sensitive cells was similar in both mouse and squirrel POA (mice: 15.2 ± 3.7%, squirrels: 15.1 ± 3.1%, p>0.05, Mann-Whitney test, Figure 1D and E).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that warm-sensitive cell proportions are similar while cold-sensitive proportions differ.

claims.claim: A population of mouse POA neurons might possess a cold-sensing mechanism that is absent in squirrel POA.
claims.source: These data suggest that a population of mouse POA neurons might possess a cold-sensing mechanism that is absent in squirrel POA.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the difference in proportions of cold-sensitive neurons between mice and squirrels.

claims.claim: Cnga3 was the most highly enriched transcript within the cold-sensitive neuronal population (14-fold enrichment).
claims.source: Transcriptome analysis of pooled cold-sensitive versus cold-insensitive mouse POA neurons revealed that the most highly enriched transcript within the cold-sensitive neuronal population was the cyclic nucleotide-gated ion channel Cnga3 (14-fold enrichment, Figure 2A and B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA sequencing data presented in Figure 2.

claims.claim: RNA in situ hybridization confirmed the expression of Cnga3 in a subset of mouse POA neurons.
claims.source: RNA in situ hybridization confirmed the expression of Cnga3 in a subset of mouse POA neurons (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA in situ hybridization data presented in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: Mice contain a population of cold-sensitive POA neurons which are enriched with CNGA3 channels.
claims.source: Together, these data reveal that mice contain a population of cold-sensitive POA neurons, which are enriched with CNGA3 channels.
claims.evidence: This is supported by transcriptomic and RNA in situ hybridization data.

claims.claim: Injection of cGMP into the POA alters the firing rate and thermosensitivity of hypothalamic neurons.
claims.source: This idea is supported by the findings that injection of the endogenous cyclic nucleotide-gated channel activator, cGMP, into the POA alters the firing rate and thermosensitivity of hypothalamic neurons and affects core body temperature in several species (Wright et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claims.claim: Injection of cGMP into the POA affects core body temperature in several species.
claims.source: This idea is supported by the findings that injection of the endogenous cyclic nucleotide-gated channel activator, cGMP, into the POA alters the firing rate and thermosensitivity of hypothalamic neurons and affects core body temperature in several species (Wright et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claims.claim: l-cis-diltiazem drastically suppressed cold activation of mouse POA neurons.
claims.source: Consistent with this, we found that l-cis-diltiazem, an inhibitor of CNGA3-containing heteromeric channels, drastically suppressed cold activation of mouse POA neurons (Figure 3A and B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental calcium imaging data presented in Figure 3.

claims.claim: l-cis-diltiazem is an inhibitor of CNGA3-containing heteromeric channels.
claims.source: Consistent with this, we found that l-cis-diltiazem, an inhibitor of CNGA3-containing heteromeric channels, drastically suppressed cold activation of mouse POA neurons (Figure 3A and B).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about the pharmacology of l-cis-diltiazem.

claims.claim: l-cis-diltiazem failed to affect calcium influx in response to depolarization by high extracellular potassium.
claims.source: At the same time, the inhibitor failed to affect calcium influx in response to depolarization by high extracellular potassium, demonstrating a specific effect on cold-sensing machinery (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental calcium imaging data presented in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: l-cis-diltiazem has a specific effect on cold-sensing machinery.
claims.source: At the same time, the inhibitor failed to affect calcium influx in response to depolarization by high extracellular potassium, demonstrating a specific effect on cold-sensing machinery (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that l-cis-diltiazem suppresses cold activation but not potassium-induced depolarization.

claims.claim: l-cis-diltiazem failed to suppress activation of warm-sensitive cells.
claims.source: Furthermore, the inhibitory effect of l-cis-diltiazem was specific to cold-sensing cells, as the drug failed to suppress activation of warm-sensitive cells (Figure 3D–F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental calcium imaging data presented in Figure 3D-F.

claims.claim: The inhibitory effect of l-cis-diltiazem is specific to cold-sensing cells.
claims.source: Furthermore, the inhibitory effect of l-cis-diltiazem was specific to cold-sensing cells, as the drug failed to suppress activation of warm-sensitive cells (Figure 3D–F).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the differential effects of l-cis-diltiazem on cold-sensitive versus warm-sensitive cells.

claims.claim: CNGA3 is necessary for cold sensitivity of mouse POA neurons.
claims.source: These data strongly indicate that CNGA3 is necessary for cold sensitivity of mouse POA neurons.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the pharmacological inhibition experiments with l-cis-diltiazem.

claims.claim: Cooling from 22°C to 12°C failed to stimulate mCNGA3 in the absence of cGMP.
claims.source: Cooling the extracellular solution from 22°C to 12°C failed to stimulate mCNGA3, demonstrating that cold alone does not activate the channel (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological recordings in Xenopus oocytes presented in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: Cold alone does not activate mCNGA3.
claims.source: Cooling the extracellular solution from 22°C to 12°C failed to stimulate mCNGA3, demonstrating that cold alone does not activate the channel (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that cooling without cGMP does not activate the channel.

claims.claim: Cooling in the presence of 1 µM intracellular cGMP led to potent and reversible activation of mCNGA3 across a wide range of voltages (4-fold activation at 60 mV).
claims.source: However, cooling in the presence of a sub-threshold concentration (1 µM) of intracellular cGMP led to potent and reversible activation of mCNGA3 across a wide range of voltages (4-fold activation at 60 mV), consistent with the idea that cold facilitates cGMP-mediated activation of the channel (Figure 4B and D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological recordings in Xenopus oocytes presented in Figure 4B and D.

claims.claim: Cold facilitates cGMP-mediated activation of mCNGA3.
claims.source: However, cooling in the presence of a sub-threshold concentration (1 µM) of intracellular cGMP led to potent and reversible activation of mCNGA3 across a wide range of voltages (4-fold activation at 60 mV), consistent with the idea that cold facilitates cGMP-mediated activation of the channel (Figure 4B and D).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that cold potentiates mCNGA3 activity in the presence of sub-threshold cGMP.

claims.claim: CNGA3 can co-assemble with CNGB1 or CNGB3 to form functional heteromeric channels.
claims.source: CNGA3 can co-assemble with CNGB1 or CNGB3 to form functional heteromeric channels with increased sensitivity to inhibition by l-cis-diltiazem compared to CNGA3 homomers (Peng et al., 2004; Peng et al., 2003; Zhong et al., 2003).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claims.claim: CNGA3-CNGB1 or CNGA3-CNGB3 heteromeric channels have increased sensitivity to inhibition by l-cis-diltiazem compared to CNGA3 homomers.
claims.source: CNGA3 can co-assemble with CNGB1 or CNGB3 to form functional heteromeric channels with increased sensitivity to inhibition by l-cis-diltiazem compared to CNGA3 homomers (Peng et al., 2004; Peng et al., 2003; Zhong et al., 2003).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claims.claim: The profound suppression of cold activation in the POA by l-cis-diltiazem suggests the presence of drug-sensitive heteromers.
claims.source: The profound suppression of cold activation in the POA by l-cis-diltiazem suggests the presence of drug-sensitive heteromers.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the pharmacological properties of l-cis-diltiazem and the observed suppression of cold activation.

claims.claim: Cngb1, but not Cngb3, is expressed in both cold-sensitive and insensitive POA neurons.
claims.source: Our transcriptomic analysis revealed that Cngb1, but not Cngb3, is expressed in both cold-sensitive and insensitive POA neurons (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA sequencing data presented in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: Co-expression of mCNGA3 with mCNGB1 led to a twofold inhibition of cold-activated current by l-cis-diltiazem compared to mCNGA3 alone.
claims.source: Co-expression of mCNGA3 with mCNGB1 led to a twofold inhibition of cold-activated current by l-cis-diltiazem compared to mCNGA3 alone (Figure 5B and C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological recordings in Xenopus oocytes presented in Figure 5B and C.

claims.claim: CNGB1 cannot form functional homomers.
claims.source: Since CNGB1 cannot form functional homomers, the drug-resistant fraction of the cold-activated current is likely due to the presence of mCNGA3 homomers (Zhong et al., 2003).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claims.claim: The drug-resistant fraction of the cold-activated current is likely due to the presence of mCNGA3 homomers.
claims.source: Since CNGB1 cannot form functional homomers, the drug-resistant fraction of the cold-activated current is likely due to the presence of mCNGA3 homomers (Zhong et al., 2003).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that some cold-activated current remains after l-cis-diltiazem treatment and the knowledge that CNGB1 cannot form homomers.

claims.claim: CNGA3-CNGB1 heteromers can form a cold-activated l-cis-diltiazem-sensitive ion channel.
claims.source: Thus, CNGA3-CNGB1 heteromers can form a cold-activated l-cis-diltiazem-sensitive ion channel.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the co-expression experiments showing increased drug sensitivity.

claims.claim: CNGA2 is a cGMP-activated ion channel.
claims.source: To test if cold activates other members of the cyclic nucleotide-gated channel family, we analysed CNGA2, a cGMP-activated ion channel (Altenhofen et al., 1991; Gordon and Zagotta, 1995; Trudeau and Zagotta, 2003), which we found to be expressed in cold-activated and cold-insensitive mouse POA neurons at similar levels (Figure 6A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claims.claim: CNGA2 is expressed in cold-activated and cold-insensitive mouse POA neurons at similar levels.
claims.source: To test if cold activates other members of the cyclic nucleotide-gated channel family, we analysed CNGA2, a cGMP-activated ion channel (Altenhofen et al., 1991; Gordon and Zagotta, 1995; Trudeau and Zagotta, 2003), which we found to be expressed in cold-activated and cold-insensitive mouse POA neurons at similar levels (Figure 6A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA sequencing data presented in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: Cold failed to activate mouse CNGA2 in oocytes in the presence of 1 µM intracellular cGMP.
claims.source: In contrast to CNGA3, cold failed to activate mouse CNGA2 in oocytes in the presence of 1 µM intracellular cGMP (Figure 6B and C), while saturating 250 µM cGMP potently activated the channel (Figure 6D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological recordings in Xenopus oocytes presented in Figure 6B and C.

claims.claim: Saturating 250 µM cGMP potently activated mouse CNGA2.
claims.source: In contrast to CNGA3, cold failed to activate mouse CNGA2 in oocytes in the presence of 1 µM intracellular cGMP (Figure 6B and C), while saturating 250 µM cGMP potently activated the channel (Figure 6D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological recordings in Xenopus oocytes presented in Figure 6D.

claims.claim: Cold activation is specific to CNGA3 among the cyclic nucleotide-gated channel family.
claims.source: This result demonstrates that cold activation is specific to CNGA3 among the cyclic nucleotide-gated channel family.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that cold activates CNGA3 but not CNGA2.

claims.claim: Cold failed to potentiate the activity of Cnga3 cloned from squirrel POA (sqCNGA3).
claims.source: Strikingly, cold failed to potentiate the activity of Cnga3 cloned from squirrel POA (sqCNGA3, Figure 4C and D), even though activation with a saturating 250 µM cGMP revealed that sqCNGA3 was abundantly expressed on the surface of the oocytes (Figure 4E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological recordings in Xenopus oocytes presented in Figure 4C and D.

claims.claim: sqCNGA3 was abundantly expressed on the surface of the oocytes.
claims.source: Strikingly, cold failed to potentiate the activity of Cnga3 cloned from squirrel POA (sqCNGA3, Figure 4C and D), even though activation with a saturating 250 µM cGMP revealed that sqCNGA3 was abundantly expressed on the surface of the oocytes (Figure 4E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological recordings showing robust currents with saturating cGMP, presented in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: Cooling from 22°C to 12°C reversibly potentiated mouse CNGA3 at positive and negative potentials in the presence of 2 µM cGMP in HEK293T cells.
claims.source: In agreement with the data from oocytes, cooling from 22°C to 12°C reversibly potentiated mouse CNGA3 at positive and negative potentials in the presence of a sub-threshold 2 µM cGMP, but failed to affect squirrel CNGA3 (Figure 7A–D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1), even though both channels were abundantly expressed on the plasma membrane, as revealed by recordings in the presence of saturating 100 µM intracellular cGMP (Figure 7E and F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological recordings in HEK293T cells presented in Figure 7.

claims.claim: Cooling from 22°C to 12°C failed to affect squirrel CNGA3 in HEK293T cells in the presence of 2 µM cGMP.
claims.source: In agreement with the data from oocytes, cooling from 22°C to 12°C reversibly potentiated mouse CNGA3 at positive and negative potentials in the presence of a sub-threshold 2 µM cGMP, but failed to affect squirrel CNGA3 (Figure 7A–D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1), even though both channels were abundantly expressed on the plasma membrane, as revealed by recordings in the presence of saturating 100 µM intracellular cGMP (Figure 7E and F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological recordings in HEK293T cells presented in Figure 7.

claims.claim: Both mouse and squirrel CNGA3 were abundantly expressed on the plasma membrane of HEK293T cells.
claims.source: In agreement with the data from oocytes, cooling from 22°C to 12°C reversibly potentiated mouse CNGA3 at positive and negative potentials in the presence of a sub-threshold 2 µM cGMP, but failed to affect squirrel CNGA3 (Figure 7A–D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1), even though both channels were abundantly expressed on the plasma membrane, as revealed by recordings in the presence of saturating 100 µM intracellular cGMP (Figure 7E and F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological recordings showing robust currents with saturating cGMP, presented in Figure 7E and F.

claims.claim: Cooling led to a robust activation of mCNGA3, with an apparent temperature threshold of 22.4 ± 0.8°C.
claims.source: Cooling led to a robust activation of mCNGA3, with an apparent temperature threshold of 22.4 ± 0.8°C, and a 10-degree activation coefficient (Q10) of 6.5 ± 0.5 (Figure 8).
claims.evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological recordings in Xenopus oocytes presented in Figure 8.

claims.claim: mCNGA3 has a 10-degree activation coefficient (Q10) of 6.5 ± 0.5.
claims.source: Cooling led to a robust activation of mCNGA3, with an apparent temperature threshold of 22.4 ± 0.8°C, and a 10-degree activation coefficient (Q10) of 6.5 ± 0.5 (Figure 8).
claims.evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological recordings in Xenopus oocytes presented in Figure 8.

claims.claim: Cold specifically and reversibly potentiates the activity of mouse, but not squirrel CNGA3 in the presence of subthreshold intracellular cGMP.
claims.source: Together, our data demonstrate that cold specifically and reversibly potentiates the activity of mouse, but not squirrel CNGA3 in the presence of subthreshold intracellular cGMP, and that this effect is independent of cell type.
claims.evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological recordings in multiple cell types.

claims.claim: The cold potentiation effect on mouse CNGA3 is independent of cell type.
claims.source: Together, our data demonstrate that cold specifically and reversibly potentiates the activity of mouse, but not squirrel CNGA3 in the presence of subthreshold intracellular cGMP, and that this effect is independent of cell type.
claims.evidence: This is supported by observations in both Xenopus oocytes and HEK293T cells.

claims.claim: Cold sensitivity of mouse POA neurons is mediated by heteromers and homomers of CNGA3.
claims.source: Our results also agree with the notion that cold sensitivity of mouse POA neurons is mediated by heteromers and homomers of CNGA3.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the pharmacological and electrophysiological data.

claims.claim: Cooling from 21.8 ± 5.48 µM at 22°C to 3.5 ± 0.63 µM at 12°C significantly decreased the half-maximal cGMP concentration (EC50) for mouse CNGA3.
claims.source: Paired recordings from the same patches at different temperatures revealed a significant decrease in half-maximal cGMP concentration (EC50) upon cooling from 21.8 ± 5.48 µM at 22°C to 3.5 ± 0.63 µM at 12°C (Figure 9C and E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by inside-out patch recordings in HEK293T cells presented in Figure 9.

claims.claim: There was no significant change in cGMP EC50 for squirrel CNGA3 upon cooling (26.4 ± 1.12 µM at 22°C, 20.4 ± 2.14 µM at 12°C).
claims.source: In contrast to mouse CNGA3, and in agreement with our whole-cell data in oocytes and HEK293T cells, we did not detected a significant change in cGMP EC50 for squirrel CNGA3 (26.4 ± 1.12 µM at 22°C, 20.4 ± 2.14 µM at 12°C, Figure 9B,D and E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by inside-out patch recordings in HEK293T cells presented in Figure 9.

claims.claim: Cooling from 22°C to 12°C at saturating (≥100 µM) cGMP concentrations inhibited maximal activity of mouse CNGA3 by 25%.
claims.source: Interestingly, cooling from 22°C to 12°C at saturating (≥100 µM) cGMP concentrations inhibited maximal activity of mouse CNGA3 by 25%, whereas this effect was significantly higher for the squirrel channel (60%, Figure 9F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by inside-out patch recordings in HEK293T cells presented in Figure 9F.

claims.claim: Cooling from 22°C to 12°C at saturating (≥100 µM) cGMP concentrations inhibited maximal activity of squirrel CNGA3 by 60%.
claims.source: Interestingly, cooling from 22°C to 12°C at saturating (≥100 µM) cGMP concentrations inhibited maximal activity of mouse CNGA3 by 25%, whereas this effect was significantly higher for the squirrel channel (60%, Figure 9F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by inside-out patch recordings in HEK293T cells presented in Figure 9F.

claims.claim: The potentiating effect of cold at low cGMP concentrations is specific to mouse CNGA3.
claims.source: Together, these findings reveal that the potentiating effect of cold at low cGMP concentrations is specific to mouse CNGA3, and is caused by a decrease in EC50 for the cyclic nucleotide.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the differential effects of cold on mouse versus squirrel CNGA3 EC50.

claims.claim: The potentiating effect of cold on mouse CNGA3 is caused by a decrease in EC50 for cGMP.
claims.source: Together, these findings reveal that the potentiating effect of cold at low cGMP concentrations is specific to mouse CNGA3, and is caused by a decrease in EC50 for the cyclic nucleotide.
claims.evidence: This is supported by the inside-out patch recordings showing decreased EC50 with cooling.

claims.claim: Cold may act by enhancing the affinity between CNGA3 and cGMP.
claims.source: We established that cold decreases the effective concentration of cGMP needed for mouse CNGA3 activation, suggesting that it acts by enhancing the affinity between the channel and the nucleotide and/or facilitating channel opening in response to nucleotide binding (James and Zagotta, 2018).
claims.evidence: This is speculated based on the observed decrease in EC50 and cited literature.

claims.claim: Cold may act by facilitating channel opening in response to nucleotide binding.
claims.source: We established that cold decreases the effective concentration of cGMP needed for mouse CNGA3 activation, suggesting that it acts by enhancing the affinity between the channel and the nucleotide and/or facilitating channel opening in response to nucleotide binding (James and Zagotta, 2018).
claims.evidence: This is speculated based on the observed decrease in EC50 and cited literature.

claims.claim: The mechanism of cold activation of mouse CNGA3 is intrinsic to the channel and does not involve cell type-specific components.
claims.source: The observation that cold activates mouse CNGA3 in various cell types strongly suggests that this mechanism is intrinsic to the channel and does not involve cell type-specific components.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that cold activates mouse CNGA3 in multiple cell types.

claims.claim: Cold acts on mouse CNGA3 even in inside-out patches.
claims.source: Furthermore, our finding that cold acts on mouse CNGA3 even in inside-out patches, and fails to increase activity of mouse CNGA2 and the squirrel orthologue of CNGA3 argues against the involvement of indirect pathways such as cold-induced augmentation of cGMP production (Chao et al., 2015; Mamasuew et al., 2010; Stebe et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is supported by inside-out patch recordings.

claims.claim: Cold fails to increase activity of mouse CNGA2.
claims.source: Furthermore, our finding that cold acts on mouse CNGA3 even in inside-out patches, and fails to increase activity of mouse CNGA2 and the squirrel orthologue of CNGA3 argues against the involvement of indirect pathways such as cold-induced augmentation of cGMP production (Chao et al., 2015; Mamasuew et al., 2010; Stebe et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological recordings.

claims.claim: The cold sensitivity of mouse CNGA3 does not involve indirect pathways such as cold-induced augmentation of cGMP production.
claims.source: Furthermore, our finding that cold acts on mouse CNGA3 even in inside-out patches, and fails to increase activity of mouse CNGA2 and the squirrel orthologue of CNGA3 argues against the involvement of indirect pathways such as cold-induced augmentation of cGMP production (Chao et al., 2015; Mamasuew et al., 2010; Stebe et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observations in inside-out patches and the specificity of cold effects.

claims.claim: The cyclic nucleotide gated ion channel Tax-4 is expressed in thermosensory neurons in C. elegans.
claims.source: A study in C. elegans showed that the cyclic nucleotide gated ion channel Tax-4 is expressed in thermosensory neurons, and that tax-4 mutants exhibit aberrant thermotaxic behavior, suggesting that thermosensitivity of mouse CNGA3 may have a deep evolutionary origin (Komatsu et al., 1996).

results.result: Mice have a significantly larger proportion of cold-sensitive POA neurons (10.0 ± 0.9%) compared to thirteen-lined ground squirrels (6.8 ± 0.8%, p<0.05), while warm-sensitive neuron proportions are similar between species. This species-specific difference in cold-sensitive neurons suggests mice possess a cold-sensing mechanism absent in squirrels.
results.evaluation: The calcium imaging data (C20-C23) with appropriate statistical testing (Mann-Whitney) demonstrates a significant species difference specific to cold-sensitive neurons (C24-C25). The sample sizes appear adequate (56 coverslips from 13 mice vs 33 coverslips from 9 squirrels), and the control comparison with warm-sensitive neurons strengthens the specificity of the finding. The inference about a mouse-specific mechanism (C26) is reasonable given the data.

results.result: CNGA3 is highly enriched (14-fold) in cold-sensitive mouse POA neurons compared to cold-insensitive neurons, as demonstrated by RNA sequencing and confirmed by RNA in situ hybridization showing CNGA3 expression in a subset of POA neurons.
results.evaluation: The transcriptomic analysis (C27) with 14-fold enrichment and statistical significance (p<0.001, GLM quasi-likelihood F-test) is supported by three biological replicates. RNA in situ hybridization (C28) provides independent validation. The methods describe appropriate quality control and normalization procedures for RNA-seq data, strengthening confidence in the enrichment finding.

results.result: Pharmacological inhibition with l-cis-diltiazem (50 µM), a specific inhibitor of CNGA3-containing heteromeric channels, drastically suppresses cold activation of mouse POA neurons without affecting potassium-induced depolarization or warm-sensitive neurons, indicating CNGA3 is necessary for cold sensitivity.
results.evaluation: The pharmacological data (C32, C34, C36) demonstrate specific suppression of cold responses with appropriate controls (high K+ and warm-sensitive cells). The specificity controls (C34-C37) are critical and well-executed. However, the conclusion of necessity (C38) is somewhat strong given this is pharmacological evidence only—genetic knockout or knockdown would provide stronger support. The drug concentration and specificity claim (C33) relies on prior literature.

results.result: Mouse CNGA3 is potentiated by cold (22°C to 12°C) in the presence of sub-threshold cGMP (1-2 µM), showing 4-fold activation with a temperature threshold of 22.4 ± 0.8°C and Q10 of 6.5 ± 0.5. This effect is cell-type independent, occurring in both Xenopus oocytes and HEK293T cells, but cold alone does not activate the channel.
results.evaluation: The electrophysiological data across multiple cell types (C39-C42, C58, C61-C62) with quantitative characterization provides strong support. The cell-type independence (C64) is demonstrated by replication in two systems. The requirement for sub-threshold cGMP (C40-C42) is well-controlled. The Q10 value of 6.5 indicates strong temperature sensitivity. Sample sizes appear adequate based on figure data points.

results.result: Squirrel CNGA3 is not potentiated by cold in either Xenopus oocytes or HEK293T cells, despite abundant surface expression demonstrated by robust currents with saturating cGMP. The EC50 for cGMP shows no significant change with cooling (26.4 ± 1.12 µM at 22°C vs 20.4 ± 2.14 µM at 12°C).
results.evaluation: The negative result for squirrel CNGA3 (C56, C59, C67) is supported by multiple experimental systems and includes the critical control showing abundant expression (C57, C60). The lack of EC50 change (C67) provides mechanistic insight. This species difference parallels the neuronal data, strengthening the overall narrative. The replication across cell types reduces concerns about artifacts.

results.result: Cold potentiation of mouse CNGA3 is mediated by a decrease in EC50 for cGMP from 21.8 ± 5.48 µM at 22°C to 3.5 ± 0.63 µM at 12°C, as measured by inside-out patch recordings. At saturating cGMP, cooling inhibits maximal activity by 25% for mouse CNGA3 versus 60% for squirrel CNGA3.
results.evaluation: The inside-out patch data (C66) provides direct mechanistic evidence with paired recordings from the same patches, which is methodologically strong. The EC50 shift is substantial (~6-fold) and statistically significant. The differential effects at saturating cGMP (C68-C69) add mechanistic detail. However, the large error bars on the 22°C EC50 for mouse CNGA3 (±5.48 µM) suggest some variability, though paired analysis mitigates this concern.

results.result: CNGA3 forms both homomers and heteromers with CNGB1 in POA neurons. Co-expression of mouse CNGA3 with CNGB1 increases l-cis-diltiazem sensitivity of cold-activated current twofold compared to CNGA3 alone, with the drug-resistant fraction likely representing CNGA3 homomers.
results.evaluation: The expression data (C46) shows CNGB1 but not CNGB3 in POA neurons. The heteromer formation (C47, C50) is supported by increased drug sensitivity, consistent with prior literature (C43-C44, C48). The inference about homomers (C49) is reasonable given CNGB1 cannot form functional channels alone. However, direct biochemical evidence of heteromer formation (e.g., co-immunoprecipitation) would strengthen this conclusion.

results.result: Cold activation is specific to CNGA3 among cyclic nucleotide-gated channels. Mouse CNGA2, which is expressed at similar levels in cold-sensitive and cold-insensitive POA neurons, is not activated by cold in the presence of 1 µM cGMP, though it responds to saturating 250 µM cGMP.
results.evaluation: The specificity control with CNGA2 (C53-C55) is important for establishing that cold sensitivity is not a general property of CNG channels. The expression data (C52) shows CNGA2 is present but not enriched in cold-sensitive neurons. The functional validation (C54) confirms the channel is properly expressed. This strengthens the claim that CNGA3 has unique cold-sensing properties.

results.result: The mechanism of cold activation is intrinsic to mouse CNGA3 and does not require cell-type-specific components or indirect pathways such as cold-induced cGMP production, as demonstrated by cold activation in inside-out patches and specificity to CNGA3 versus CNGA2 and squirrel CNGA3.
results.evaluation: The inside-out patch data (C75) provides strong evidence against indirect mechanisms by isolating the channel from cellular machinery. The specificity arguments (C76-C77) based on CNGA2 and squirrel CNGA3 controls further support a direct mechanism. The inference (C74) is well-justified by the combined evidence. This addresses an important mechanistic question about whether cold acts directly on the channel.

results.result: Cold may act by enhancing the affinity between CNGA3 and cGMP and/or facilitating channel opening in response to nucleotide binding, as suggested by the decreased EC50 for cGMP activation.
results.evaluation: These are speculative mechanistic interpretations (C72-C73) based on the EC50 data. While the decreased EC50 is well-established, distinguishing between increased binding affinity versus enhanced gating cooperativity would require additional experiments (e.g., direct binding assays, single-channel recordings, or structural studies). The authors appropriately frame these as possibilities rather than definitive conclusions.

results.result: The correspondence between the proportion of cold-sensitive POA neurons and cold sensitivity of CNGA3 across mice and squirrels suggests CNGA3 acts as a hypothalamic cold sensor important for detecting cold temperatures in the POA.
results.evaluation: The correlation between neuronal cold sensitivity and CNGA3 properties across species (C81) provides strong circumstantial evidence. The pharmacological necessity data (C38) and enrichment in cold-sensitive neurons (C27) support this conclusion. However, the claim that CNGA3 'acts as' a cold sensor (C8) would be more definitively supported by genetic loss-of-function experiments in vivo, which the authors acknowledge in C99-C100.

results.result: A small fraction of squirrel POA neurons exhibits cold sensitivity despite cold-insensitive CNGA3, suggesting a CNGA3-independent cold-sensing mechanism that could be important for monitoring body temperature during hibernation.
results.evaluation: The observation of residual cold-sensitive neurons in squirrels (C84, 6.8%) is supported by the calcium imaging data. The inference of a CNGA3-independent mechanism (C85) is logical given squirrel CNGA3 is cold-insensitive. However, the speculation about hibernation monitoring (C86) is reasonable but not directly tested. This represents an interesting observation that warrants future investigation.

results.result: CNGA3-expressing cold-sensitive neurons in mice could be part of the mechanism orchestrating thermogenesis in response to body cooling, while in squirrels this mechanism is expected to be inhibited to allow core body temperature drop during torpor.
results.evaluation: These are speculative physiological interpretations (C82-C83) about the role of CNGA3 in thermoregulation. While the speculation is reasonable given the known physiology of hibernation (C83 based on knowledge), there is no direct evidence linking CNGA3 to thermogenic responses or torpor. The authors appropriately frame C82 as 'a tantalizing possibility.' In vivo functional studies would be needed to test these hypotheses.

results.result: The apparent activation threshold for homomeric CNGA3 (22.4°C) is lower than physiological brain temperature, but may depend on cellular environment and recording conditions. Temperature sensitivity of hypothalamic neurons is plastic and modulated by multiple factors, and CNGA3's impact on excitability will depend on expression level and cellular properties.
results.evaluation: The acknowledgment of the threshold issue (C88) is important and appropriately caveated with citations to similar phenomena in other thermosensitive channels. The discussion of plasticity (C89, supported by citations) and context-dependence (C90, based on general principles) provides appropriate nuance. This addresses a potential concern about physiological relevance while acknowledging limitations.

results.result: The thermosensitivity of mouse CNGA3 may have a deep evolutionary origin, as suggested by the expression of the cyclic nucleotide-gated channel Tax-4 in C. elegans thermosensory neurons and aberrant thermotaxis in tax-4 mutants.
results.evaluation: This evolutionary speculation (C80) is based on cited work in C. elegans (C78-C79). While the parallel is interesting, the evidence for evolutionary conservation is indirect. Functional characterization of Tax-4 temperature sensitivity and phylogenetic analysis would be needed to support this claim more strongly. The authors appropriately frame this as a suggestion rather than a conclusion.

results.result: Further understanding of CNGA3's role in thermoregulation requires conditional ablation in adult mouse POA and/or targeted disruption of cold-sensing capability while preserving cGMP sensor function.
results.evaluation: These are appropriate suggestions for future work (C99-C100) that acknowledge the limitations of the current study. The complex phenotype of global Cnga3 knockout (C95-C98) justifies the need for conditional approaches. These represent logical next steps to establish physiological relevance, though they are speculative about experimental design rather than claims about current results.
